writeup: TIC 273026743 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected in TESS photometry with an orbital period of 5.565453 days. The system shows a primary eclipse with 2.14% dimming and a secondary eclipse detected at 6.3 sigma significance, indicating two stars orbiting each other. The automated analysis achieved a very high detection signal-to-noise ratio of 1982.1, and pixel-level imaging confirmed the source with a peak signal-to-noise of 42.8, though the centroid offset of 5.2 arcsec warrants further investigation. The target does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a previously uncatalogued candidate. One consideration: alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, a pattern that suggests the true orbital period is double the initial measurement, which has been corrected in this report.
